questions.question_text: When completing the speaking portion of the test, what is the best practice to follow?
options: Read your response from a pre-written script
Speak naturally and clearly into your microphone
Speak as quickly as possible to save time
Avoid answering the prompt if you are unsure of the answer
questions.explanation: The test evaluates natural English speaking ability, so clear, spontaneous speech is the intended approach.

questions.question_text: During the speaking section, what is the impact of speaking too softly?
options: The microphone may not pick up your voice clearly for evaluation
You get a bonus for sounding calm
The system allows more time to record
It is preferred by the examiners
questions.explanation: Clear, audible speech is necessary for the AI and human raters to accurately assess your fluency and pronunciation.

questions.question_text: What happens if you use filler words like 'um' and 'uh' excessively?
options: It helps you sound like a native speaker
It shows you have a large vocabulary
It negatively impacts your fluency score
It is ignored by the grading system
questions.explanation: Excessive use of filler words suggests a lack of confidence and fluency in the English language.

questions.question_text: When asked to speak about a specific topic for 60 seconds, what is a good strategy?
options: Stop talking as soon as you have said two sentences
Prepare a basic structure: introduction, body, and conclusion
Speak as fast as possible to include more information
Ask the system to provide you with notes
questions.explanation: A structured response is easier to follow and demonstrates your ability to organize thoughts coherently under pressure.

questions.question_text: Why should you avoid reading a pre-written script during the speaking section?
options: It is allowed but not recommended
It makes your speech sound unnatural and reduces your score
It is illegal to have paper on your desk
It consumes too much battery
questions.explanation: The speaking section aims to assess natural, spontaneous communication, not your ability to read aloud.

questions.question_text: If you are asked to describe a picture, what should you aim for?
options: Only describing the colors in the picture
Speaking in a natural rhythm, explaining what you see
Remaining silent to avoid mistakes
Translating the picture into another language
questions.explanation: The goal is to describe the visual information fluently and accurately to show you can articulate observations clearly.

questions.question_text: What is the best practice to follow during the speaking section?
options: Speak as quickly as possible.
Speak clearly at a natural, steady pace.
Whisper so others in your house don't hear.
Use very complex words even if you aren't sure of their meaning.
questions.explanation: Natural, clear speech is easier for the AI to analyze and score accurately.

questions.question_text: What is the impact of speaking too softly?
options: It shows you are being polite.
It might prevent the microphone from capturing your response correctly.
It makes you sound more intelligent.
It allows you more time to think.
questions.explanation: Clear audio input is vital for the scoring engine to understand your language usage.

questions.question_text: What is the consequence of using filler words like 'um' and 'uh' too much?
options: It increases your score.
It interrupts the flow of speech and makes it harder to understand.
It counts as part of the word limit.
It has no impact at all.
questions.explanation: Excessive fillers negatively affect the 'Fluency' component of your speaking score.

questions.question_text: What is a good strategy when speaking about a topic for 60 seconds?
options: Start with an introduction, discuss the main points, and conclude.
Repeat the same sentence for the entire minute.
Stop speaking after 30 seconds to be safe.
Read a prepared speech about a different topic.
questions.explanation: Structuring your response helps you stay on track and maintain coherence throughout the time limit.

questions.question_text: Why should you avoid reading a script during the speaking section?
options: The proctor will ask you to read it aloud.
It sounds unnatural and the score will be lower because of it.
You are not allowed to look at your computer screen.
The microphone will turn off if you read.
questions.explanation: The test measures natural speaking ability, and reading scripts is easily detectable.

questions.question_text: If asked to describe a picture, what should you aim for?
options: Identifying the colors and shapes only.
Speaking clearly about what is happening and the context of the image.
Naming every single object you see.
Describing what you think is behind the camera.
questions.explanation: A complete description includes context and action, not just a list of items.

questions.question_text: What is the best practice during the speaking section?
options: Speak as quickly as possible.
Speak clearly at a natural, steady pace.
Whisper to avoid being overheard by others.
Speak only in short, one-word answers.
questions.explanation: Clarity and a natural rhythm are better for evaluation than extreme speed or volume.

questions.question_text: What happens if you use filler words (e.g., 'um', 'uh') excessively?
options: They count as bonus words.
They can disrupt the flow of your speech and lower your fluency score.
The system ignores them completely.
They make your speech sound more natural.
questions.explanation: Excessive fillers suggest a lack of vocabulary or preparation, which impacts the fluency aspect of the speaking score.

questions.question_text: What is a good strategy for a 60-second speaking topic?
options: Pause for 30 seconds to think before starting.
Organize your thoughts quickly and keep speaking until the time is nearly up.
Read a prepared script from your screen.
Talk about three different topics to show range.
questions.explanation: A well-organized, continuous response demonstrates proficiency better than a disjointed one.

questions.question_text: Why should you avoid reading a pre-written script?
options: It is easy to detect and will cause you to fail the section.
It is too difficult to type beforehand.
It takes too much time to prepare.
The computer cannot understand written text.
questions.explanation: Academic integrity and testing rules strictly forbid scripts; the test evaluates spontaneous speech.

questions.question_text: What should you aim for when describing a picture?
options: Describing as many objects as possible regardless of logic.
Speaking in full, detailed sentences that explain the scene logically.
Using only simple 'There is/There are' sentence structures.
Describing the picture in the past tense only.
questions.explanation: Describing the scene in a descriptive, logical way shows command over vocabulary and sentence structure.

questions.question_text: If you lose your train of thought while speaking, what should you do?
options: Stay silent until the timer ends.
Briefly pause, take a breath, and try to rephrase or continue.
Start the entire answer from the beginning.
Apologize to the computer for a full minute.
questions.explanation: Staying calm and continuing is better than giving up; small pauses are natural in speech.

questions.question_text: How can you improve your speaking score?
options: By mimicking an accent that is not your own.
By speaking about a variety of topics and using diverse vocabulary.
By memorizing the questions from a previous exam.
By speaking as loudly as possible throughout the test.
questions.explanation: Using a wide range of words and demonstrating the ability to speak on different subjects shows true language mastery.
